about: Poetry journals checked by hand against each journal's own guidelines or submission page. Blank means not confirmed. Focus tags appear only where the journal says so itself. payPerPoem is the least one short poem earns. Pen Pal downloads newer versions of this list from GitHub; your own copies of journals are never changed without asking. Always read the guidelines before you send.

journals.name: The Acentos Review
journals.note: Poetry, fiction, memoir, translation and art by Latinx writers. Three to five poems in any style, and a one-line answer to "To me, being Latinx means..." in the cover letter. Translations to or from Spanish and Indigenous languages welcome.

journals.name: The Adroit Journal
journals.note: Up to six poems, and no more than two submissions per genre in a reading period. Its windows move from year to year, so check the site.

journals.name: AGNI
journals.feeNote: Free by mail
journals.note: Boston University's magazine, in print twice a year and online weekly. Usually answers in two to four months.

journals.name: Alaska Quarterly Review
journals.note: Founded 1982; traditional and experimental styles, and the editors encourage new and emerging writers. Short windows by genre each season; poetry's fall 2026 window is December 5 to 20.

journals.name: The American Poetry Review
journals.note: Philadelphia's poetry tabloid since 1972: poems, translations, essays and interviews. Submit online or by mail with a stamped envelope. Answers in about six months.

journals.name: Apalachee Review
journals.note: Volunteer-run Tallahassee journal that comes out about once a year and is always looking for work by unpublished writers. Three to five poems, September 1 to December 31.

journals.name: Appalachian Review
journals.note: Appalachian State's quarterly. One to five poems of nearly any aesthetic, if they are truly original. Only one submission at a time. Check Submittable for when it is open.

journals.name: The Arkansas International
journals.feeNote: Waivers for BIPOC writers and anyone who needs one
journals.note: University of Arkansas journal with an international reach. From fall 2026 the unthemed fall issue is online and the themed spring issue is in print too. Check Submittable for open dates.

journals.name: Atlanta Review
journals.note: Poetry journal with no school: lyric, narrative, experimental, formal, prose poems. If no form shows during a reading period, they have hit their cap. Answers in about six months.

journals.name: Barely South Review
journals.note: Old Dominion University's journal. Two windows, for the winter and spring issues. Up to three poems in one document.

journals.name: Beloit Poetry Journal
journals.feeNote: Free until 800 arrive in a month
journals.note: Five poems or one long poem. The free open periods close after 800 submissions. Publishing since 1950.

journals.name: Bennington Review
journals.note: Twice-yearly print journal for writing that is graceful and reckless at once. Three to five poems in one file. Its 2026 window ran January 5 to March 15.

journals.name: Black Fox Literary Magazine
journals.note: Twice-yearly magazine with two long windows. Submit in only one category per period.

journals.name: Black Warrior Review
journals.feeNote: Small fee, waived on request
journals.note: Often decides after a window closes, so replies can bunch up. Email them for a fee waiver if you need one.

journals.name: Chapter House Journal
journals.note: From the Institute of American Indian Arts MFA. Strongly encourages Native American, First Nations and Indigenous writers, Black and Brown writers, LGBTQ+ and disabled writers. Twice a year online.

journals.name: The Cincinnati Review
journals.paysNote: $30 a page in print; $25 for a miCRo post
journals.note: Print windows open the first of September, December and May and close when they fill. Up to five poems, ten pages. The online miCRo series takes poems of 32 lines or fewer most of the year.

journals.name: Cola Literary Review
journals.feeNote: Free September 15 to October 14; $3 from October 15 to November 15
journals.note: University of South Carolina's journal. Reads September 15 to December 15, free for the first month. Free and paid submissions are read the same way.

journals.name: The Common
journals.feeNote: Subscribers send free all year; a fee-free week each August; hardship waivers by email
journals.note: Amherst College's journal of place. Up to five poems. Especially encourages Black, Indigenous, disabled, LGBTQIA+, immigrant and low-income writers. Poetry is closed to non-subscribers for fall 2026 while they make a translation issue.

journals.name: Copper Nickel
journals.note: Send 4 to 6 poems. Poetry closes early once it reaches its submission cap, so send near the start of a window.

journals.name: Crab Creek Review
journals.note: Looks for originality, risk-taking and craft. Up to four poems, eight pages, one batch a period. The window closes early if the cap fills.

journals.name: DMQ Review
journals.note: One of the longest-running online poetry journals (27 years), never with fees. Its current focus is the prose poem; the latest window ran through October 31, 2026.

journals.name: Ecotone
journals.feeNote: A free window opens first each period until 250 come in; subscribers and mail are free
journals.note: Dedicated to reimagining place, with room for climate and natural history. Reading periods usually start in late winter and late summer, plus a Valentine's Day window; dates move, so check. Three to five poems.

journals.name: Faultline
journals.note: UC Irvine's journal of arts and letters. One window a year, October 15 to December 15, capped at 250 poetry submissions. Once a year per genre; they answer by late spring.

journals.name: FLARE: The Flagler Review
journals.note: Flagler College's journal in St. Augustine. Open September 30 to January 15; up to five poems in one document, one submission per genre.

journals.name: The Florida Review
journals.feeNote: Small online fee
journals.note: UCF's journal, in print and online as Aquifer. Its Editor's Prizes ($25 entry, $1,000 award) run Jan 1 to Apr 15.

journals.name: Folio
journals.note: American University's journal. Volume 42, the Whimsical Issue, reads October 15 to December 15, 2026. Up to five poems.

journals.name: Frontier Poetry (New Voices)
journals.feeNote: A paid two-week fast reply is optional
journals.note: New Voices is free and open all year to poets with no more than two full-length books. Up to five poems, ten pages. Its contests are separate and charge fees.

journals.name: The Georgia Review
journals.feeNote: Free for subscribers and by mail
journals.note: University of Georgia's quarterly since 1947. Send up to 10 pages; they often run several pages by one poet. Aims to answer within ten months.

journals.name: The Greensboro Review
journals.note: UNC Greensboro's journal. General submissions November 1 to January 1, for the fall issue; acceptances go out in May.

journals.name: Gulf Coast
journals.note: The whole $3 fee goes to paying the writers they publish.

journals.name: Gulf Stream Magazine
journals.note: FIU's online journal, two issues a year, often with a theme. Current FIU students can't submit; alumni can two years after graduating.

journals.name: Harvard Review
journals.feeNote: Hardship waivers by email
journals.note: Harvard's journal of fiction, poetry and essays, open to writers at every stage. No more than five poems. Its reading dates are not posted on the guidelines page, so check Submittable.

journals.name: Hayden's Ferry Review
journals.feeNote: Free queues for underrepresented writers each issue
journals.note: Arizona State's international journal. Up to three poems, eight pages, for print; web issues have themes. Translations are open all year. Each issue has its own window (Issue 80 closes December 1).

journals.name: The Hudson Review
journals.feeNote: By mail, with a stamped return envelope
journals.note: Poetry by mail only, April 1 to June 30 (postmarked). Up to seven poems; no simultaneous submissions. Translations welcome, and poets at every stage are encouraged.

journals.name: iO: A Journal of New American Poetry
journals.note: Poetry journal that takes most of its poems from open submissions. One reading period a year, September 1 to December 1, up to five poems. Answers in two or three months.

journals.name: The Iowa Review
journals.feeNote: Subscribers send one free
journals.note: Poetry window is August 1 to October 1. Up to 8 pages, one poem or several, read blind. Answers in one to six months.

journals.name: The Journal
journals.note: Ohio State's journal. Up to three poems in one file. Loves traditional forms and experimental, hybrid work alike. Reopened November 15, 2026; the closing date is not posted. Allow eight months.

journals.name: The Kenyon Review
journals.note: A short September window. Up to six poems in one document, one genre per reading period. They aim to answer within six months.

journals.name: Kweli Journal
journals.note: Online journal for writers of color, four issues a year. Up to three poems, six pages in one file.

journals.name: The Margins (Asian American Writers' Workshop)
journals.note: AAWW's magazine, for emerging and established Asian American and diasporic poets, in English or in translation. Up to five pages, any style. Moving poems into online issues from late 2026. Check Submittable for open dates.

journals.name: The Massachusetts Review
journals.feeNote: Free by mail
journals.note: Quarterly of literature, art and public affairs since 1959. Up to six poems; most run under 100 lines. Closed May through September.

journals.name: The Missouri Review
journals.note: Reads all year. Each issue runs three poetry features, so send 8 to 20 pages, not single poems. Answers in 10 to 12 weeks.

journals.name: Narrative Magazine
journals.paysNote: $200 at least per poem; $100 for reprints
journals.note: Reads all year. Up to five poems that show your range, in any form; no translations. Pays at least $200 a poem and takes some reprints.

journals.name: Naugatuck River Review
journals.note: Founded to publish narrative poetry, in the line of Patricia Smith, Philip Levine and James Wright. Two reading periods a year, summer and winter; the winter issue is a contest issue.

journals.name: New England Review
journals.feeNote: Free by mail or with a subscription
journals.note: Closes early once it hits its cap. In fall 2026 poetry closed on September 4, so send on day one.

journals.name: New Ohio Review
journals.feeNote: Submittable lists a fee for regular submissions; subscribers can send more often
journals.note: Ohio University's journal, two print and two online editions a year. Up to six pages of poems, once a reading period; cross-genre and unusually formatted work welcome. Answers in two to four months.

journals.name: Nimrod International Journal
journals.note: University of Tulsa's international journal. General submissions in April and November; up to seven pages of poems, one poem per page.

journals.name: Ninth Letter
journals.feeNote: Free in December until 300 come in
journals.note: University of Illinois journal. Print reads September through February; the web edition opens September 1 to November 1 and February 1 to April 1. Three to five poems, eight pages.

journals.name: Northwest Review
journals.note: Revived Oregon journal that wants formally inventive, experimental work, writers from marginalized communities, and writers who have never been published. Check Submittable for open dates.

journals.name: Obsidian: Literature & Arts in the African Diaspora
journals.note: Black, African and African diaspora writers. Up to five poems, eight pages. The general issue has read May 15 to Oct 15; watch for themed calls.

journals.name: The Offing
journals.feeNote: No fees in 2026, thanks to donors
journals.note: Online magazine for work that challenges and experiments, and a place for new writers to test their voices. One to five poems of any form or length. Check Submittable for when poetry is open.

journals.name: Palette Poetry
journals.feeNote: Featured Poetry is free; a quick-reply option is offered for marginalized writers
journals.note: Online journal that strongly encourages new and emerging poets and publishes only from its open windows. Check Submittable for when Featured Poetry is open.

journals.name: The Paris Review
journals.note: Poetry opens on Submittable in January, April, July and October until it fills, and by mail all year. Up to six poems, no more than twice a calendar year. Translations welcome with the original. Answers take six to eight months.

journals.name: Plenitude Magazine
journals.feeNote: $3 CAD for US and international poets; none listed for Canadians
journals.note: Canada's magazine for LGBTQ2S+ writers, with a particular welcome for BIPOC, trans and disabled writers. Up to five pages of poetry. Closed in December.

journals.name: Ploughshares
journals.feeNote: Free by mail or for subscribers
journals.note: Send 3 to 5 pages of poetry. One submission per reading period. Spring and summer issues have guest editors.

journals.name: Poet Lore
journals.note: America's oldest poetry journal, since 1889. Always free. Up to five poems, ten pages. Answers take about six to eight months.

journals.name: Poetry
journals.note: Poetry Foundation's monthly, publishing since 1912. Two to six poems, up to ten pages. One submission at a time; closed June 15 to September 15. Answers within about eight months.

journals.name: Poetry Northwest
journals.feeNote: The Presenting category for poets not yet in a national print journal is free
journals.note: Twice-yearly print issues plus the web. Up to four poems, once a reading period. General poetry reopens March 1 to 31, 2027; the Presenting feature opens separately for newer poets.

journals.name: Poetry South
journals.note: Annual poetry journal that pays particular attention to poets born, raised or living in the South, alongside poets from anywhere. One to four poems; long poems considered. Deadline July 15 for that year's issue.

journals.name: Porchlight
journals.note: A journal of Southern literature that welcomes the range of Southern voices, emerging and established. Three to five poems, ten pages. Reading periods change each year, so check Submittable.

journals.name: Prairie Schooner
journals.note: Two short windows a year that can close early when they hit their cap. Five to seven poems in one document, and no simultaneous submissions. Especially welcomes writers of color.

journals.name: Qu
journals.feeNote: Waivers by email
journals.note: Queens University of Charlotte's magazine. One to three poems for the winter issue, October 15 to January 15. Pays US contributors.

journals.name: Raleigh Review
journals.note: Nonprofit magazine of accessible, emotionally and intellectually complex work. Poetry is open January 1 to April 1 and July 1 to October 31.

journals.name: Rappahannock Review
journals.note: University of Mary Washington's online journal. Its 2026 window ran July 31 to September 1 for issue 14.1; check for the next one.

journals.name: Rattle
journals.note: Open all year and always free. Poems of any length. Publishes about 300 poems a year, nearly all unsolicited.

journals.name: River & South Review
journals.note: Twice a year, for work that gets a visceral reaction. Especially welcomes Black, Indigenous, Latine, Asian and South Asian writers, LGBTQIA+ writers, disabled writers and older writers.

journals.name: Rust & Moth
journals.note: Four short windows a year. Uses web-length lines, so very long lines may need reworking.

journals.name: Saw Palm
journals.note: Florida literature and art, from the University of South Florida. Writers from anywhere are welcome if the work is connected to Florida, and Floridians may send work about anything. Open July 1 to October 1.

journals.name: Shenandoah
journals.note: Washington and Lee's journal. Three to five of your most urgent poems, ten pages; the editor reads for power, surprise and risky strangeness. Poetry next opens January 15, 2027, for the first 200 submissions.

journals.name: Shō Poetry Journal
journals.feeNote: Free portals for BIPOC poets, and always free for US Indigenous poets
journals.note: Poetry journal with free submission portals for BIPOC poets and a standing free portal for US Indigenous poets. Up to five unpublished poems; only one submission pending at a time.

journals.name: South Florida Poetry Journal (SoFloPoJo)
journals.note: Reads poetry all year and publishes in February, May, August and November; each issue closes six weeks before it comes out. Answers in four months or less. Runs a yearly prize for LGBTQIA+ poets.

journals.name: Southeast Review
journals.feeNote: Fees go to the contributors’ fund; a free category for BIPOC poets
journals.note: Florida State's journal, twice a year plus SER Online, with emerging writers next to established ones. Open in fall and spring; up to five poems, 15 pages.

journals.name: Southern Humanities Review
journals.feeNote: A limited free category closes after 100 submissions
journals.note: Auburn University's journal. Up to three poems, then wait for an answer before sending more. Translations welcome with the original and permission. Check Submittable for open dates.

journals.name: The Southern Review
journals.paysNote: $75 for the first page, $25 a page after, up to $300
journals.note: LSU's quarterly since 1935. Up to five poems, 15 pages at most, and no more than two submissions a period.

journals.name: Southword
journals.note: From the Munster Literature Centre in Cork. Poetry is open every January for up to four poems, and closes early if 1,000 submissions arrive.

journals.name: Split Lip Magazine
journals.feeNote: Tip-jar submissions; free all year for Black writers
journals.note: Voice-driven journal with a pop culture twist, online monthly. Open in February, April, June, August, October and early December; Black writers can submit free in any month except July and late December.

journals.name: Spoon River Poetry Review
journals.note: Illinois State's poetry journal. Free reading period every year, September 1 to February 28. All kinds of poetry, including translations, multilingual poems and long poems up to ten pages.

journals.name: storySouth
journals.note: Online journal with two windows a year, June 15 to July 15 and December 15 to January 15. Three to five poems; long pieces are encouraged. Answers in two to six months.

journals.name: Strange Horizons
journals.note: Weekly magazine of speculative work. Poems with a science fiction, fantasy, horror, myth, supernatural or science element. Poetry is open all year; up to six poems. Answers within four months.

journals.name: The Sun
journals.note: Ad-free monthly. Caps submissions each month. Buys one-time print and online rights.

journals.name: SWWIM Every Day
journals.feeNote: Some submission options carry a fee
journals.note: A poem every weekday by women and gender-expansive writers, run from Miami. After publishing with them, wait six months to send again.

journals.name: Tampa Review
journals.note: University of Tampa's journal. One to five poems; answers in about 12 to 16 weeks. Currently reading for a Florida Man issue alongside general submissions.

journals.name: Tar River Poetry
journals.note: East Carolina University's poetry journal, now free to read online. Up to five poems in one Word file, from emerging and established poets. The fall 2026 window is open for the spring 2027 issue.

journals.name: THINK
journals.note: Publishes mainly metrical poetry, plus nonce forms and free verse with a clear organizing principle. Up to five poems in one Word file, no PDFs.

journals.name: Third Wednesday
journals.note: Quarterly that reads everything blind. No more than three poems, once a quarter. Answers in three months or less, often much sooner.

journals.name: The Threepenny Review
journals.note: Reads Jan 1 to Apr 15 only. Rights go back to you on publication. Online submitters who hear nothing for two weeks should take it as a no.

journals.name: Tinderbox Poetry Journal
journals.feeNote: Free in March and September until the cap; tip-jar options otherwise
journals.note: Welcomes new and emerging voices; four issues a year on the solstices and equinoxes. Free reading periods are usually March and September and close at the cap.

journals.name: Torch Literary Arts
journals.note: Publishes Black women writers, especially work that disrupts what writing by Black women is expected to be. Rolling submissions for Friday Features, no fee. Up to five poems, eight pages.

journals.name: Uncanny Magazine
journals.note: Science fiction and fantasy magazine that wants passionate, experimental speculative poems of any length, each sent separately. Closed right now with no reopening date posted; it answers in about 30 days when open.

journals.name: Unsplendid
journals.note: Online journal, three times a year, for poems in received forms (sonnets, villanelles, ghazals, blank verse, prose poems and more) and invented nonce forms. Translations in traditional forms welcome.

journals.name: Waxwing
journals.note: Caps at 300 submissions a month across genres. If the form is closed, try again on the 1st.

journals.name: The Yale Review
journals.note: Reads poetry in September until it reaches its cap, and answers everyone by the end of May. Often publishes new voices first found in its queue.

journals.name: ZYZZYVA
journals.note: San Francisco print journal since 1985, looking for California writers first but open to everyone. Closed now; the next window is to be announced in late 2026.
